text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Paged KV metadata growth detected in prod-us-west-2 cluster at 2026-02-17T03:12:01Z. Indexer backlog rising, block_manager.metadata.size increased 4x in 10m, continuous-batch latency spike. Auto-escalation to #eng-runtime oncall. :rotating_light:
Amelia: grabbing this now. I see the alert, pulling logs and the block manager metrics dashboard.
Amelia: initial impact: 20% of requests to /v1/generate are seeing >2000ms tail latency, a few 502s reported from downstream proxy. Customer impact: small but visible across a handful of mid-tier tenants (acct: acme-corp, devtools-inc).
Dan: thanks — any immediate rollback or config flip we can do?
Amelia: proposing immediate mitigations: 1) reduce continuous_batch.max_tokens to 128 globally for affected pool; 2) temporarily disable kv.prefetch for the paged pools; 3) force a gentle eviction by reducing block_manager.eviction_threshold to 0.6 to free up metadata.
Anita: those are good. Which pool specifically?
Amelia: pool: rwinf-prod-paged-usw2-01 (GPU pool id p-78a).
Mike: I can patch the runtime config and push a canary. Will do the config change as a feature-flagged rollout to 5% first.
Amelia: please add a reminder to monitor cache hit ratio, metadata growth, and continuous_batch queue length.
Mike: executing now. Patch:
```
# patch to runtime config
continuous_batch:
  max_tokens: 128
  max_wait_ms: 12
kv_paged:
  prefetch_enabled: false
block_manager:
  eviction_threshold: 0.6
  eviction_policy: lru
```
DeployBot: deploy queued by Mike to pool rwinf-prod-paged-usw2-01, canary=5%. CI checks passed.
Mike: canary deployed at 03:17 UTC. Observing metrics...
Amelia: early signs: continuous_batch queue depth down ~30%, tail latency down ~15% in the canary hosts. Metadata growth rate still positive but slowed.
Dan: what about long-term root cause? This spike looks like a metadata leak pattern — maybe a block size mismatch with a new model variant that increased kv block headers. Any recent model switches?
Sara: ops note: we rolled out model v2.9.1 to the default route yesterday evening; larger tokenizer chunking has been suspected. I've opened an eval job to compare block footprint between v2.9.0 and v2.9.1.
Anita: good catch. If v2.9.1 increases block header count (smaller blocks), that explains metadata blowup. We should consider a temporary model pin for affected customers and a long-term blocksize tuning.
Amelia: for immediate scope: 1) expand canary to 25% if canary metrics hold for 5m, 2) notify Customer Success for the affected accounts, 3) start a follow-up ticket for a permanent fix (block size + model tokenization changes).
Mike: canary -> 25% at 03:25 UTC. Metrics: tail latency improved further, error rate back to baseline in canary. Rolling to 100% in 10m if stable.
Dan: also add a DC-routing fallback policy: if metadata size > X, route to a dedicated non-paged pool to avoid paged-kv thrash — as a short-term safety valve.
Amelia: created an emergency route rule in the routing layer: if block_manager.metadata.size > 1.2GB on a host, start diverting new sessions to dedicated pool rwinf-prod-dedicated-usw2 as of 03:30 UTC.
DeployBot: routing change applied to us-west-2 edge plane.
Amelia: CS notified: @cs-team please proactively reach out to Acme and DevTools, summary in #customer-success. Ticket: CS-5542 created.
Sara: eval results: v2.9.1 increases average block metadata per model by ~3.7x for certain prompt patterns with long system tokens. Repro is in sandbox.
Dan: that aligns. Proposed postmortem actions: - model pin to v2.9.0 for default route until model tokenization fix, - tune block_size up from 4KB to 16KB for paged pools to reduce metadata overhead, - add a metadata leak detector alert to our runbook.
Amelia: agreed. For now, canary rollback not needed; we have stable metrics after config changes. Still seeing some hosts with high disk IO from eviction churn. I'm going to trigger a controlled eviction sweep to free top percentile of cold blocks.
Mike: performing eviction sweep command:
```
# runtime admin
runtimectl host p-78a evict-cold-blocks --threshold=90 --rate=50
```
Amelia: sweep started at 03:38 UTC. Monitoring.
Mike: sweep completed at 03:41 UTC. Freed ~18GB metadata across canary hosts. Disk IO spike was within expected safe limits.
Amelia: expanding config rollout to 100% at 03:45 UTC. Continuous_batch queue length normalized, tail latency returned to baseline, error rate under SLA.
Dan: excellent. Next steps: 1) longer-term tuning ticket for block_size and eviction heuristics (ENG-RT-3129), 2) model team to investigate tokenization change in v2.9.1 (ENG-ML-2210), 3) add a runbook entry for paged-kv metadata surges and automated routing fallback.
Anita: I'll own ENG-RT-3129. ETA 72h for investigation and a safe experiment plan (blocksize experiments on canary), will coordinate with ML.
Sara: I'll follow up with the model team on ENG-ML-2210, we'll try a candidate patch to reduce header expansion.
Amelia: closing incident if no regressions for next 1 hour. Leaving thread open for handoff to Anita for the tuning ticket.
Amelia: final notes for the handoff: root-cause suspected model tokenization change + paged-kv block sizing interaction. Immediate mitigations: reduce continuous batch size, disable prefetch, lower eviction threshold, routing fallback. Customers notified and CS ticket created.
Anita: acknowledged, taking ownership of post-incident ticket. Adding folks to the ticket: Dan, Mike, Sara, Amelia.
Mike: logs and metric snapshots uploaded to ENG-RT incident folder: s3://rwinf-incidents/1765554321/
DeployBot: incident summary posted to #incidents-manual with link to timeline.
Amelia: oncall handoff: I'm off in 40m. Anita will take over monitoring and postmortem. Good job team. :thumbsup:
